A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Residual-MPPI. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original MuJoCo experiments with RL and imitation-learning priors, GTS racing experiments, and trajectory analyses.

after.justification: V5 reports original benchmark results, parameter and dynamics ablations, tire-transfer experiments, and a Prompt-DT comparison.

M1.justification: The core sampling, log-prior-plus-add-on objective, importance-weighted action update, and dynamics training/fine-tuning design are retained. V5's deployment Algorithm 2 documents the pipeline already described in v1; revised experimental rewards and hyperparameters do not introduce a new planner component.

E1.justification: V5 adds a Race-Hard-to-Race-Soft tire-transfer scenario in GTS and an ANT-dir comparison using multidirectional expert demonstrations. The original four MuJoCo customization objectives, RL/GAIL prior coverage, and racing task remain.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 10 add Greedy-MPPI, Valued-MPPI and Residual-SAC to the MuJoCo comparisons; Table 1 also adds Fulltask-SAC. GTS newly evaluates Full-MPPI, Guided-MPPI and Greedy-MPPI, while Appendix F.6 adds evaluated Prompt-DT variants.

E3.justification: GTS planning changes from horizon 4, 3000 samples and top ratio 0.002 to 15, 500 and 0.048; Equation 26 replaces the fixed 7.3 boundary threshold with position-dependent course width. Table 3 revises prior-network architecture, discount, learning rate and batch size. New protocols include budget-matched SAC checkpoints, 100-episode/10-lap ablations and alternative Prompt-DT prompt constructions.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's trajectory examples and zero/few-shot comparison, v5 tests removal of the log-prior objective, sensitivity to five planning parameters, and dynamics training components. Figures 9–17 and Tables 11–12 add extensive sensitivity, component-ablation and tire-shift evidence; Figure 3 adds baseline failure cases.

E5.justification: V1 Table 2 reports GTS values with ± notation without identifying the uncertainty measure; v5 explicitly identifies mean ± standard deviation. Main evaluation counts remain 500 MuJoCo episodes and 30 GTS laps. No new seed-based replication, confidence-interval estimation or significance-testing procedure is described.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 10 replace numerous scores and add comparative results. Table 2 changes few-shot GTS results from 120.75 seconds/36.60 off-course steps to 122.93 seconds/4.43 steps under revised settings, so this is not a controlled performance gain. V5 also adds ablation, transfer and Prompt-DT outcomes, while omitting v1's numerical mean/maximum off-course distances.

T1.justification: Appendix A generalizes Lemma 1's trajectory factorization from an optimal maximum-entropy policy to an arbitrary policy under deterministic dynamics. The main maximum-entropy result and its derivation are otherwise retained; changing its main-text label from Theorem to Proposition is not itself a mathematical change.

C1.justification: The abstracts and introductions retain the central contribution: online continuous-control policy customization using prior action distributions without the original reward or additional policy training, demonstrated in zero/few-shot settings and GTS. Additional comparisons and analyses support this retained claim.

C2.justification: V5 substantially expands explanations of Greedy-MPPI's reward trade-offs, Valued-MPPI's objective mismatch, and sensitivity to planning parameters and dynamics error. It interprets tire-transfer results as motivation for future sim-to-real use and explicitly discusses the domain gap. Existing limitations concerning prior quality, dynamics accuracy and terminal values remain.

D1.justification: V5 adds deployment pseudocode, discloses GTS dynamics-training horizon 5 and discount 1, and clarifies the MuJoCo exploration-noise source. It adds statements about MuJoCo code and supplementary evaluation logs, whose availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Most hardware and implementation documentation already appeared in v1.

R1.justification: Beyond consolidating v1's extended related work, v5 explicitly attributes the MPPI/maximum-entropy relationship to Bhardwaj et al. and develops comparisons with MBOP, LOOP, Ceil and Prompt-DT. It sharpens distinctions between customization, offline planning and policy adaptation, while removing several peripheral citations.

P1.justification: V5 substantially rewrites experimental setup and results discussions, organizing MuJoCo findings around three comparative advantages. It consolidates extended related work into Section 6, revises the abstract and limitations narrative, and restructures the appendices around a deployment section and six additional-results subsections.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 10 gain grouped comparator rows, and Table 2 gains a failed-baseline block. V5 adds Tables 11–14 and Figures 3, 6 and 9–17, redraws GTS route plots, relocates retained visualizations, and adopts the ICLR page and header layout.

improvement.justification: V5 substantially addresses v1's limited comparative and mechanistic validation through stronger baseline controls, training-budget comparisons, component ablations, parameter sensitivity and tire-transfer tests. These clarify when the method helps and where it remains limited; attribution and deployment documentation also improve. Reporting inconsistencies remain, notably Section 4.2's 2K dynamics-training steps versus Table 4's 200K, but the added validation provides a substantial net quality gain.
